question.problem:
$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the vectors shown above. Given that the inner product in the vector space ${R}^{3}$ is defined as 

$$
⟨x,y⟩=3{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+2{x}_{3}{y}_{3},
$$

which of the following statements are true?

I. ${v}_{1}⊥{v}_{2}$ with respect to the given inner product

II. ${v}_{2}⊥{v}_{3}$ with respect to the given inner product

III. $S=\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}\}$ is an orthogonal set with respect to the given inner product

choices.value: None of the statements are true
